items.claim: Atmospheric cold plasma (ACP) treatment modifies the structure and properties of ferritin to allow subunit dissociation and reassembly at a milder pH (pH 4.0) for encapsulation.

citation.title: Ferritin Nanocage: A Versatile Nanocarrier Utilized in the Field of Food, Nutrition, and Medicine
citation.authors: Chenxi Zhang, Xiaorong Zhang, Guanghua Zhao

provenance.span: Atmospheric cold plasma (ACP) treatment affects the tryptophan microenvironment around ferritin channels, decreases alpha-helix/beta-sheet contents, and lowers aromatic surface hydrophobicity and thermal stability, thereby facilitating dissociation into subunits at a more benign pH (pH 4.0) for guest molecule encapsulation.

items.claim: Pulsed electric field (PEF) treatment modifies ferritin structure to allow dissociation at a milder pH (pH 3.6).

citation.title: Ferritin Nanocage: A Versatile Nanocarrier Utilized in the Field of Food, Nutrition, and Medicine
citation.authors: Chenxi Zhang, Xiaorong Zhang, Guanghua Zhao

provenance.span: Pulsed electric field (PEF) treatment modifies the structure and features of ferritin, enabling it to dissociate at a milder pH (pH 3.6) for encapsulation.

items.claim: MTS treatment decreases ferritin stability and allows encapsulation of guest molecules via mild pH conversion.

citation.title: Ferritin Nanocage: A Versatile Nanocarrier Utilized in the Field of Food, Nutrition, and Medicine
citation.authors: Chenxi Zhang, Xiaorong Zhang, Guanghua Zhao

provenance.span: Manothermosonication (MTS) treatment decreases ferritin stability, affecting iron oxidative deposition and release activity, allowing apoferritin to encapsulate EGCG via a benign pH conversion (pH 3.0/6.8).

items.claim: Thermal treatment at up to 60 °C expands the fourfold channels of phytoferritin to allow cargo loading.

citation.title: Ferritin Nanocage: A Versatile Nanocarrier Utilized in the Field of Food, Nutrition, and Medicine
citation.authors: Chenxi Zhang, Xiaorong Zhang, Guanghua Zhao

provenance.span: Temperature changes (heating up to 60 °C) can expand the fourfold channels of phytoferritin, as evidenced by an increased initial iron release rate and decreased alpha-helix content, allowing guest molecules to be loaded through channel expansion and recovery.

items.claim: High hydrostatic pressure alters protein conformation by impairing hydrophobic interactions to allow encapsulation.

citation.title: Ferritin Nanocage: A Versatile Nanocarrier Utilized in the Field of Food, Nutrition, and Medicine
citation.authors: Chenxi Zhang, Xiaorong Zhang, Guanghua Zhao

provenance.span: High hydrostatic pressure (HHP) treatment (200–300 MPa) impairs hydrophobic interactions and changes tertiary and quaternary structure to encapsulate DOX into human H-chain ferritin without protein precipitation.

items.claim: Elastin-like polypeptides undergo a reversible inverse phase transition (co-acervation/self-aggregation) from soluble protein into insoluble hydrophobic aggregates (forming beta-spiral structures with type II beta-turns) when heated above their transition temperature (Tt), or through high local concentrations in the ER, leading to the formation of protein bodies.

citation.title: Induction of protein body formation in plant leaves by elastin-like polypeptide fusions
citation.authors: Andrew J Conley, Jussi J Joensuu, Rima Menassa, Jim E Brandle

provenance.span: ELP fusion tags and elastin-like polypeptides

items.claim: Fluorescence complementation is directly proportional to α-synuclein solubility because the small GFP11 sensor fragment can only complement with the large GFP1–10 detector fragment if α-synuclein escapes aggregation and remains soluble, exposing the sensor fragment to the solvent.

citation.authors: Ahmed Kothawala, Kiri Kilpatrick, Jose Andres Novoa, Laura Segatori

items.claim: Impairing MinE membrane interaction (via truncation or single mutations in the membrane targeting sequence) increases MinD ATPase stimulation and reduces the lower limit of the concentration-dependent wavelength.
